title: Figurative language sort cards
subject: English
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 46 (Figurative language sort cards (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 46: Grammar: simile, metaphor and personification. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Simile
Metaphor
rows: The market was like a beehive.

panels.title: Personification
points: Gives a human action or feeling to a thing
The wind whispered at the window.
The old house sighed as the door shut.
Makes a setting feel alive or threatening

cards: Her voice was as soft as wool.
The sun smiled on the playground.
The kettle grumbled on the stove.
blocks.title: Sort into: Simile / Metaphor / Personification
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Simile, Metaphor, Personification.
blocks.answer: Simile: Her voice was as soft as wool.; He ran like the wind.. Metaphor: The city was a beehive.; Britain is a recipe.. Personification: The sun smiled on the playground.; The kettle grumbled on the stove.

model.title: Describe a busy market in three sentences.

parts.text: Metaphor: The market was a river of voices.
Personification: Crates of mangoes waited patiently in the sun.
Simile: Spices glowed like small fires in their sacks.
Check: every image fits the same mood

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The market was a river of voices. Crates of mangoes waited patiently in the sun, and spices glowed like small fires in their sacks.

keywords.def: giving human qualities to something that is not human
words that create a picture in the reader's mind
meaning exactly what the words say

questions.q: Label: 'The night wrapped the town in a blanket.' Which device, and what is the effect?
questions.a: Personification (and metaphor): night acts like a carer, so the town feels safe and quiet.

questions.q: Turn the simile into a metaphor: 'The playground was like a battlefield.'

Core: in the portal response box, write a descriptive paragraph about your street or a place where many people meet, using at least two metaphors and one personification. Starter: 'Every morning my street...'
questions.a: A paragraph with two metaphors and one personification, each fitting the mood.

questions.q: Extend: underline each device and write its name in the margin
Stretch: write an extended metaphor of three sentences that keeps one image going
questions.a: For example: the school as a ship: the head teacher steers, the corridors are decks, the bell is the ship's horn.

questions.q: 'The classroom was a zoo.' This is...
questions.a: A) a metaphor. It says the classroom IS a zoo, without 'like' or 'as'.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: which is more powerful, 'like a beehive' or 'is a beehive'? Why?
questions.a: For example: 'is a beehive', because the metaphor is bolder and more vivid.
